leads.name: Granny Pine over An Lochan Uaine (Glenmore)
leads.note: Cairngorms Connect (cairngormsconnect.org.uk/news/191/37/Cailleach-Hag-Granny-Queen) says a granny pine over the lochan still stands, hundreds of years old, twisted arms. One source, no girth, no tree-level pin (lochan coordinate is approximate, from memory of the site, not verified). Needs a geotagged Commons/Geograph photo of the trunk or a OSM node to ship.
leads.species_basis: genus read from the tree's own name; ask the reader which species

leads.name: Peter Porter (Craigmore, Abernethy)
leads.note: Historic: 'In the Shadows of Cairngorm' ch.38 (electricscotland.com/history/cairngorm/38.htm, 19th-century author) names one of the largest pines at Craigmore, about 300 years old / 80 ft / 14 ft girth, ring count 243 plus missing centre. No sign it still stands, no coordinate. Do not ship unplaced.

leads.name: The Queen (Rothiemurchus, near Dell gate by the Moss)
leads.note: Same book, ch.38: 'a splendid specimen of the ancient pine'. No size, age, coordinate, nothing recent. Cairngorms Connect also mentions a 'Queen of the Forest' in Abernethy whose whereabouts are unknown. Possibly the same legend; unplaceable.
